rationale: The sandbox is a single-tenant microVM. AgentCore validates the Cognito authorization header and the adapter verifies a binding token against the Cognito subject hash on every invocation, so tenancy is enforced by the transport, not by route filtering.
/api/chat and /api/terminal already grant arbitrary in-sandbox execution, so filtering feature routes buys no isolation while breaking the product.
Upstream 0.2.0 registers 496 /api/* routes and its browser bundle references 308 route families. An enumerated allowlist cannot track that surface: every gap surfaces as a 403 on a working feature.
Only credential-minting and lifecycle-seizing routes stay denied. None of them are called by the upstream browser bundle, so denying them removes no functionality.

unavailablePrefixes.reason: Host-native desktop control; not registered by upstream 0.3.0 and impossible inside a microVM.

deniedPrefixes.reason: GET /api/token/local mints a dashboard session token for same-host callers holding the local secret. The supervisor already holds that token and the browser must never receive it.
Defensive alias so a future rename of the token family cannot silently become reachable.
Defensive: no secret-bearing family may become reachable by upstream rename.
Defensive: a full config export would carry MCP credentials and model API keys into browser storage.
The supervisor owns gateway lifecycle; a browser-initiated exit is indistinguishable from a crash and races checkpoint/restore.

Upstream 0.3.0 registers POST /api/restart (and the dev-fleet app's /api/restart-gateway). The supervisor owns gateway lifecycle: a browser-initiated restart races checkpoint/restore exactly like /api/shutdown.
